actions.justification: Mandatory first step — patient is tachycardic at HR 140 with elevated BP; full vital signs assessment is required before any treatment decisions.
Mandatory per guidelines — ECG required before rate control initiation; confirms AF and evaluates for accessory pathways or other arrhythmias contributing to tachycardia.

Mandatory — patient on chronic amiodarone presenting with weight loss, tremor, and tachycardia; TSH is critical to evaluate for amiodarone-induced thyrotoxicosis which would alter management strategy.
MANDATORY: CHA2DS2-VASc score must be calculated to guide anticoagulation decisions in this patient with persistent AF and tachycardia (HR 140).
MANDATORY: Basic metabolic panel needed to assess electrolytes, renal function, and metabolic status, which are critical before initiating rate control therapy and in the context of amiodarone use.
Patient has HR of 140 with elevated BP; continuous cardiac monitoring is essential to track rate response and detect any arrhythmic deterioration while assessment and workup proceed.

Mandatory per ESC AF guideline - patient has persistent AF with HR 140 and needs anticoagulation risk stratification. CHA2DS2-VASc score assessment already done; formal anticoagulation need assessment is required next.

Rate control is indicated for HR 140 in stable AF. Beta blocker is preferred rate control agent; amiodarone should be avoided given suspected amiodarone-induced thyrotoxicosis (weight loss, tremor, tachycardia on chronic amiodarone). BP 155/90 and SpO2 97% support safe administration.

Complex case with suspected amiodarone-induced thyrotoxicosis causing AF with rapid ventricular response. Cardiology input needed for management of amiodarone toxicity and rhythm/rate control strategy.

Guideline contraindicates rate control without ECG confirmation. Although 12-lead ECG was obtained, ordering a repeat/formal ECG ensures current rhythm documentation before any additional rate control interventions, and satisfies the guideline requirement.

ESC AF guideline mandates rate control as the initial strategy for stable AF. HR is 140 bpm and the patient is on chronic amiodarone with symptoms of possible amiodarone-induced thyrotoxicosis; additional rate control is needed while awaiting TSH results.

ESC AF guideline requires assessment and initiation of anticoagulation for AF. CHA2DS2-VASc assessment was already completed; anticoagulation should be initiated to reduce thromboembolic risk in this patient with persistent AF.

Chest X-ray is indicated to assess for pulmonary complications of chronic amiodarone use (pulmonary toxicity) and to evaluate cardiac size in this patient with persistent AF and new systemic symptoms.

Echocardiogram is indicated to assess structural heart disease, left atrial size, and ventricular function in a patient with persistent AF and recurrent symptoms, guiding further management decisions.

Electrophysiology consultation is warranted given recurrent AF symptoms on chronic amiodarone therapy with new signs of amiodarone toxicity (weight loss, tremor, tachycardia), to evaluate rhythm control strategy and amiodarone alternatives.
CBC is indicated to evaluate for anemia or infection contributing to tachycardia and AF symptoms, and to assess overall hematologic status in the context of anticoagulation therapy.
Renal function assessment is important for dosing decisions and evaluating amiodarone-related organ toxicity, as well as guiding anticoagulation management.

Echocardiogram is indicated to assess cardiac structure and function, evaluate for amiodarone-related cardiomyopathy, and guide rate/rhythm control strategy in this patient with recurrent AF and new systemic symptoms.
Patient has tachycardia (HR 140) and persistent AF — NT-proBNP helps assess heart failure contribution and guides management decisions.
Patient is on chronic amiodarone which affects anticoagulation metabolism; INR is needed to assess current anticoagulation status and guide dosing.
Coagulation profile is indicated to assess bleeding risk and anticoagulation adequacy in this patient with AF on amiodarone who has already received anticoagulation.
Patient has sustained tachycardia (HR 140) with AF; troponin is indicated to rule out myocardial injury or demand ischemia in the setting of rapid ventricular response.
With HR 140 and MAP 105, assessing lactate helps evaluate for tissue hypoperfusion and guides further management decisions.

Patient remains tachycardic at HR 140 despite prior rate control/beta-blocker. A non-dihydropyridine calcium channel blocker (e.g., diltiazem) is indicated as adjunct rate control in AF per ESC AF guidelines. IV amiodarone should be avoided given suspected amiodarone-induced thyrotoxicosis.
